dossier.purpose: Apple's open-source (Apache-2.0) Swift CLI and launchd-managed helper services for building and running Linux containers from OCI images on Apple-silicon Macs. Each container runs in its own lightweight VM (Apple Virtualization framework, driven through the external `Containerization` package) attached to vmnet networks. It also provides image build (BuildKit in a builder VM), registry login, named volumes, user-defined networks, persistent 'container machines' that mount the host home directory, and an experimental local Kubernetes plugin. Host platform scope is macOS only; Linux appears only as the guest OS inside the VMs.

claims.claim: `container` creates and runs Linux containers as lightweight virtual machines on a Mac; it is written in Swift and optimized for Apple silicon.
Consumes and produces OCI-compatible images: pull from any standard registry, push built images, and run them in other OCI-compatible applications.
Uses the apple/containerization Swift package for low-level container, image and process management.
You need a Mac with Apple silicon to run `container`.
Supported on macOS 26 (new virtualization and networking features); older macOS versions are not supported and maintainers typically will not address issues that cannot be reproduced on macOS 26.
Install by downloading the latest signed installer package from the GitHub release page, double-clicking it and entering an administrator password so files are placed under /usr/local.
Start the system service with `container system start`.
`container run --rm alpine echo hello` pulls alpine, runs it in a lightweight Linux VM, prints hello and removes the container on exit.

Upgrade, downgrade and uninstall use the signed pkg or the update-container.sh / uninstall-container.sh scripts installed to /usr/local/bin; the service must be stopped first with `container system stop`; `-k` keeps and `-d` removes user data.
Under active development; release versions are product versions, not semantic versions.
CLI compatibility is generally preserved within a major release; features marked experimental (for example the `k8s` subcommand) may change and carry no backward-compatibility guarantee.
The `container-apiserver` XPC API keeps forward and backward compatibility within a major version; other non-public XPC helpers carry no CLI or API compatibility guarantee across versions.
Application data has forward compatibility only, guaranteed within one major version; upgrading to a newer major version may require a specific upgrade path.

install.method: macOS signed installer package from GitHub Releases (GUI installer)
install.command: Download the latest signed .pkg from https://github.com/apple/container/releases, double-click it and enter the administrator password (installs under /usr/local); then run: container system start

install.method: Upgrade/downgrade with the bundled update script
install.command: container system stop; /usr/local/bin/update-container.sh   # downgrade: /usr/local/bin/uninstall-container.sh -k && /usr/local/bin/update-container.sh -v 0.3.0; then: container system start

install.method: Build from source and install to /usr/local (Apple silicon Mac, macOS 15+ with 26 recommended, Xcode 26)
install.command: BUILD_CONFIGURATION=release make all test integration && BUILD_CONFIGURATION=release make install

install.method: Claude Code skill plugin (teaches the CLI; does not install the tool itself)
install.command: /plugin marketplace add apple/container   then   /plugin install container@apple-container

platforms.linux_x86_64: no. macOS-only: Package.swift:30 declares only `.macOS("15")`; README.md:18 requires a Mac with Apple silicon; docs/command-reference.md:1327 says system commands are only available on macOS hosts; the runtime imports Virtualization and vmnet (Sources/Services/RuntimeLinux/Server/NonisolatedInterfaceStrategy.swift:23-24, Sources/Services/NetworkVmnet/Server/ReservedVmnetNetwork.swift:25-26) and uses launchd (Sources/ContainerPlugin/ServiceManager.swift:21-45). No Linux-host build, install doc or CI job exists; CI runs on [self-hosted, macos, tahoe, ARM64] (.github/workflows/common.yml:27). Linux is only the guest OS.
platforms.wsl2: no. No WSL or Windows reference anywhere in the repo (case-insensitive grep over md/swift/yml/toml/json). The runtime depends on macOS-only Virtualization.framework, vmnet, XPC, launchd and Keychain (Sources/ContainerXPC/XPCServer.swift:17 is wrapped in `#if os(macOS)`; Sources/Services/ContainerImagesService/Server/ImagesService.swift:426 uses KeychainHelper), none of which exist under WSL2.
platforms.macos_arm64: yes. README.md:18-20 (Apple silicon, macOS 26 supported). Package.swift:30 sets a macOS 15 minimum with reduced functionality (docs/technical-overview.md:61-75): `container network` is registered only on macOS 26+ (Sources/ContainerCommands/Application.swift:179-192) and non-default networks need macOS 26 (Sources/Services/ContainerAPIService/Client/Utility.swift:300-305). Default kernel and default --arch are arm64 (Sources/ContainerPersistence/ContainerSystemConfig.swift:170; docs/command-reference.md:46); the CLI refuses to run under Rosetta (Application.swift:168-176). Intel Macs are unsupported per README.md:18.
platforms.gpu: no. No GPU, Metal or graphics-device flag or code in Sources/ or docs/ (case-insensitive grep for GPU|Metal|graphics|VZVirtioGraphics|CUDA found only an SVG DTD string). VM device setup is delegated to the external Containerization package, which was not inspected.

integrations.cli: yes. `container` binary (Sources/CLI/ContainerCLI.swift:19-24; executable target Package.swift:76-84) with command groups container/image/builder/network/volume/machine/registry/system/k8s (Sources/ContainerCommands/Application.swift:45-98; docs/command-reference.md). Machine-readable output via `--format json|table|yaml|toml` on list/inspect-style commands (docs/command-reference.md:856; docs/container-inspection.md:7-60).
integrations.mcp: none found. No MCP server, config or mention (case-insensitive grep for mcp / model context protocol over all md/swift/json/yml/toml returned nothing).
integrations.sdk_or_api: Swift libraries over XPC; no HTTP/REST API found. 24 SwiftPM library products (Package.swift:31-56) including ContainerAPIClient; `ContainerClient` and `NetworkClient` are XPC clients of Mach service `com.apple.container.apiserver` (Sources/Services/ContainerAPIService/Client/ContainerClient.swift:29-37; NetworkClient.swift:41; server Sources/APIServer/APIServer+Start.swift:91-97). XPC callers must share the server's EUID (Sources/ContainerXPC/XPCServer.swift:175-193). API docs: https://apple.github.io/container/documentation/ (README.md:94). The apiserver serves XPC plus loopback DNS on 127.0.0.1:2053 and :1053 (APIServer+Start.swift:38-40).
integrations.claude_code_or_codex: Claude Code: a skill-only plugin. `.claude-plugin/plugin.json:19-21` (skills: ./skills/container), `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json:7-14`, install via `/plugin marketplace add apple/container` and `/plugin install container@apple-container` (skills/README.md:22-27). The skill teaches the CLI surface and the Docker-to-container mapping and loads on demand (skills/container/SKILL.md:1-47; skills/README.md:3-5,29-30). No hooks, MCP server or command-sandboxing wrapper found. Codex: none found (no AGENTS.md or .codex files).

readme.telemetry_and_network:
Telemetry: none found. No analytics or crash-reporting code or SDK (case-insensitive grep for telemetry|analytics|sentry|crashlytics|phone home found nothing relevant; direct dependencies in Package.swift:57-74 include no analytics package; swift-metrics and swift-distributed-tracing appear only as transitive pins, Package.resolved:139-147,193-201). Logs go to the macOS unified log or, with --log-root, local files (docs/command-reference.md:1343-1348; docs/logs.md:48-63). No automatic update check in the CLI; the user-run update script calls api.github.com and downloads the pkg (scripts/update-container.sh:101-110,153-160). README.md:1-110 says nothing about telemetry or network policy.
Accounts and required network: no account needed; registry login is optional and stored in the macOS Keychain (Sources/Services/ContainerAPIService/Client/Constants.swift:19-20; Sources/ContainerCommands/Registry/RegistryLogin.swift:63-96). First `container system start` pulls ghcr.io/apple/containerization/vminit:<tag> (ContainerSystemConfig.swift:147-153; Sources/ContainerCommands/System/SystemStart.swift:153-155,166-175) and, after a Y/n prompt or --enable-kernel-install, downloads a Kata Containers kernel tarball from github.com (ContainerSystemConfig.swift:168-171; SystemStart.swift:177-201), verified against a pinned SHA-256 (Sources/Services/ContainerAPIService/Server/Kernel/KernelService.swift:125-131,184-196). Images default to registry docker.io (ContainerSystemConfig.swift:241-243; ClientImage.swift:112-113); builds need ghcr.io/apple/container-builder-shim/builder:0.13.1 (ContainerSystemConfig.swift:84-87; Package.swift:25); `k8s` pulls docker.io/kindest/node (Sources/ContainerK8s/K8sHelper.swift:39). Proxy environment variables and CONTAINER_* variables are passed to helper services (Sources/ContainerPlugin/PluginLoader.swift:239-244,311-318).
Host listeners and changes: XPC Mach service plus DNS on 127.0.0.1:2053/1053; `-p` without a host IP binds 0.0.0.0 (Sources/Services/ContainerAPIService/Client/Parser.swift:659-672; Tests/ContainerAPIClientTests/UtilityTests.swift:128); `sudo container system dns create` writes /etc/resolver and, with --localhost, /etc/pf.conf anchors and restarts mDNSResponder (Sources/ContainerCommands/System/DNS/DNSCreate.swift:56-91; Sources/Services/ContainerAPIService/Client/PacketFilter.swift:23-26,112-147; docs/host-integration.md:54-57). A macOS Local Network Privacy prompt may be triggered (Sources/ContainerOS/LocalNetworkPrivacy.swift:20-33).

entry_points.what: Root swift-argument-parser command registering the Container/Image/Machine/Volume/Builder/Network/System groups; unknown subcommands fall through to the plugin loader; `network` group only on macOS 26+
`container-apiserver` launchd agent: XPC Mach service com.apple.container.apiserver plus DNS resolvers on 127.0.0.1:2053 and :1053
`container-runtime-linux`: per-container XPC helper that boots the VM (logic in Sources/Services/RuntimeLinux/Server/RuntimeService.swift)
`container-network-vmnet`: XPC service managing a vmnet network
`container-core-images`: XPC service managing OCI images and the content store
`k8s` plugin entry point (experimental local Kubernetes clusters)

code.architecture: CLI -> client library -> XPC -> launchd-managed helpers. `Sources/CLI/ContainerCLI.swift` runs the command tree in `Sources/ContainerCommands/` (Container/, Image/, Builder/, Network/, Volume/, Machine/, System/, Registry/). Commands parse flags in `Sources/Services/ContainerAPIService/Client` (Parser.swift, Utility.swift, Flags.swift; ContainerClient and NetworkClient XPC clients over `Sources/ContainerXPC`) and call `container-apiserver` (`Sources/APIServer`; services in `Sources/Services/ContainerAPIService/Server`: Containers, Networks, Volumes, Kernel, Plugins, DiskUsage). `container system start` registers the apiserver as a per-user launchd agent (SystemStart.swift:115-130; Sources/ContainerPlugin/ServiceManager.swift:124-136). The apiserver loads helpers through `Sources/ContainerPlugin` (PluginLoader): `container-core-images` (`Sources/Services/ContainerImagesService`), `container-network-vmnet` (`Sources/Services/Network*`, vmnet shared or host mode), `machine-apiserver` (`Sources/Services/MachineAPIService`), the experimental `k8s` plugin (`Sources/ContainerK8s`), and one `container-runtime-linux` per container (docs/technical-overview.md:47). That runtime service builds the VM with `VZVirtualMachineManager` from the external Containerization package (RuntimeService.swift:175-180), attaches virtiofs, ext4 and tmpfs mounts and vmnet interfaces, and applies capabilities and masked/read-only paths. The guest runs vminitd (external), reached over vsock gRPC (docs/logs.md:36-39). Image builds use `Sources/ContainerBuild` (gRPC to a BuildKit builder VM). Support modules: `Sources/DNSServer`, `Sources/SocketForwarder` (published ports), `Sources/ContainerPersistence` (config.toml), `Sources/ContainerResource` (resource models), `Sources/TerminalProgress`.
code.packaging_and_release: Artifacts: `container-installer-unsigned.pkg` (pkgbuild, identifier com.apple.container-installer, install-location /usr/local; Makefile:34,160-173) and `container-dSYM.zip` (Makefile:175-187); the package stages bin/container, bin/container-apiserver, libexec/container/plugins/*, update-container.sh and uninstall-container.sh (Makefile:127-158). Binaries are ad-hoc code-signed (`codesign --force --sign -`, Makefile:37,163-169); only container-runtime-linux and container-network-vmnet carry an entitlement, `com.apple.security.virtualization` (signing/*.entitlements:5-6). The release workflow (.github/workflows/release.yml:7-9,23-57) triggers on tags N.N.N, builds through common.yml, then creates a draft GitHub prerelease named `<tag>-prerelease` with only the .zip and .pkg. No checksums, SBOM, notarization, Sigstore or build-provenance attestations in any workflow or the Makefile (grep for attest|cosign|sigstore|sha256sum|notar|provenance|SBOM found nothing relevant). README.md:24 and scripts/update-container.sh:126-149 refer to a `container-installer-signed.pkg` whose production is not in this repo; the update script falls back to the unsigned pkg after a prompt and does no integrity check beyond HTTPS (update-container.sh:153-160). Libraries are consumable via SwiftPM (Package.swift:31-56); DocC API docs are deployed to GitHub Pages (.github/workflows/docs-release.yml:31-46).
code.tests_and_ci: Framework: Swift Testing (`import Testing`, `@Test`/`@Suite`); 112 files import it and no file uses XCTest. About 117 Swift test files: 67 unit files in 14 targets under `Tests/*Tests` (ContainerAPIClientTests, ContainerBuildTests, ContainerPersistenceTests, ContainerPluginTests, ContainerResourceTests, DNSServerTests, SocketForwarderTests and others; Package.swift:85-594) plus 50 CLI integration files in `Tests/IntegrationTests` (Build, Containers, Images, K8s, Machine, Network, Registry, Run, System, Volumes, Warmup); about 1,170 `@Test` markers. `make test` runs unit tests only (Makefile:189-191); `make integration` starts the real apiserver, installs the kernel and runs warmup, concurrent and serial suites against live VMs (Makefile:281-318). The only `withKnownIssue` in the tree is the host-only network test (Tests/IntegrationTests/Network/TestCLINetwork.swift:126-128). CI workflows in .github/workflows: common.yml (reusable: hawkeye/swift-format check, protobuf drift check, `make container dsym docs`, `make test install-kernel integration` or coverage; runs only when github.repository == 'apple/container' on `[self-hosted, macos, tahoe, ARM64]`, lines 25-27,39-112); pr-build.yml (signed-commit check plus build with coverage); merge-build.yml (push to main and release/*); release.yml (tag to draft prerelease); docs-release.yml (manual GitHub Pages deploy); pr-coverage-comment.yml; pr-label-analysis.yml and pr-label-apply.yml. Dependabot updates github-actions weekly (.github/dependabot.yml:1-12). Most actions are pinned by commit SHA; docs-release.yml:46 uses the tag `actions/deploy-pages@v5`.
code.dependencies: Package.swift declares 16 direct SwiftPM packages (lines 57-74): apple/containerization (`exact: 0.47.0`), swift-argument-parser, swift-collections, swift-configuration, swift-log, swift-nio, swift-protobuf, swift-system, grpc-swift-2, grpc-swift-nio-transport, grpc-swift-protobuf, async-http-client, swift-docc-plugin, mattt/swift-toml, mattt/swift-configuration-toml and jpsim/Yams; all but containerization use `from:` ranges. Package.resolved pins 35 packages (16 direct plus 19 transitive such as swift-crypto, swift-nio-ssl, swift-certificates, facebook/zstd), each by git revision. No other dependency manifests exist. Toolchain: Swift 6.2 tools (Package.swift:1) and Xcode 26 (BUILDING.md:7); CI uses Xcode_swift_6.3 (common.yml:32). At runtime it also fetches a Kata kernel tarball, the vminit and builder-shim OCI images, and the kindest/node image (see telemetry_and_network).
code.security_policy: none. No SECURITY.md in the repo root, .github/ or docs/; no vulnerability-reporting text found (case-insensitive grep for security@|vulnerab|security policy|responsible disclosure returned nothing). CONTRIBUTING.md:3 and MAINTAINERS.txt:3 only link to apple/containerization; the issue-template config offers only GitHub Discussions (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml:2-5).

claim_checks.claim: Linux containers run as lightweight VMs, one VM per container (README.md:6; docs/technical-overview.md:26-28,47).
claim_checks.evidence: The apiserver launches a `container-runtime-linux` helper per container (docs/technical-overview.md:47; Package.swift:408-425). RuntimeService.bootstrap builds a `VZVirtualMachineManager` VM with kernel, init filesystem and per-container mounts and networks (Sources/Services/RuntimeLinux/Server/RuntimeService.swift:175-180,188-222). The strength of isolation rests on Apple Virtualization.framework and the external Containerization package (README.md:10), which were not audited.

claim_checks.claim: macOS 26 is the supported OS and older macOS is not supported (README.md:20).
claim_checks.evidence: Code and other docs still allow macOS 15: Package.swift:30 `.macOS("15")`; BUILDING.md:6 'macOS 15 minimum, macOS 26 recommended'; docs/technical-overview.md:61-75 describes macOS 15 operation with limits. macOS 26 gates: `container network` (Application.swift:179-192), non-default networks (Utility.swift:300-305), reserved vmnet networks (@available(macOS 26) at ReservedVmnetNetwork.swift:29). Code wins: macOS 15 runs with reduced network features.

claim_checks.claim: The release is distributed as a signed installer package (README.md:24).
claim_checks.evidence: The repo builds `container-installer-unsigned.pkg` with pkgbuild and ad-hoc `codesign --sign -` (Makefile:34,37,163-173); release.yml:44,55-57 uploads the *.pkg and *.zip to a draft prerelease; there is no productsign, notarization or checksum step. scripts/update-container.sh:126-149 looks for `container-installer-signed.pkg` and falls back to unsigned after a prompt, so a signed pkg must be produced outside this repo (not checkable here).

claim_checks.claim: Each VM mounts only the data you share ('Privacy', docs/technical-overview.md:29, linked from README.md:91).
claim_checks.evidence: `container run` mounts only what flags request (-v/--mount/--tmpfs/--ssh/--publish-socket; Sources/Services/ContainerAPIService/Client/Utility.swift:163-188,247-251). But `container machine` mounts the user's home read-write by default (docs/command-reference.md:1093; docs/container-machine.md:73), and ContainersService.swift contains no mount allow-list; validateMount only checks the path is absolute and exists (Parser.swift:597-619).

claim_checks.claim: A separately created network is isolated and `--internal` restricts it to host-only (docs/networking.md:155-176; docs/command-reference.md:805).
claim_checks.evidence: `--internal` maps to NetworkMode.hostOnly and then vmnet VMNET_HOST_MODE (Sources/ContainerCommands/Network/NetworkCreate.swift:31-32,68; ReservedVmnetNetwork.swift:114). Default and plain networks are NAT with outbound access (Sources/ContainerResource/Network/NetworkMode.swift:19-22; APIServer+Start.swift:325-331). The only integration test of external blocking is marked `withKnownIssue("curl error 7 despite retries", isIntermittent: true)` (Tests/IntegrationTests/Network/TestCLINetwork.swift:126-128,166-174). Enforcement is delegated to Apple vmnet; the repo has no firewall or egress policy.

claim_checks.claim: Containers start with a restricted capability set and OCI-default masked and read-only paths (docs/runtime-configuration.md:8-10,55-63).
claim_checks.evidence: Capability math is in RuntimeService.swift:1317-1346 and flags are validated in Parser.swift:1049-1079, with tests in Tests/IntegrationTests/Run/TestCLIRunCapabilities.swift. The default set includes CAP_NET_RAW, CAP_DAC_OVERRIDE and CAP_MKNOD (docs/runtime-configuration.md:10). Default masked/read-only path lists come from the external Containerization package (`LinuxContainer.defaultMaskedPaths()`, Parser.swift:1093,1099) and whether each applies depends on the guest kernel (Tests/IntegrationTests/Run/TestCLIRunSecurityPaths.swift:38-43); the path flags are EXPERIMENTAL (Flags.swift:298-302,347-351). No seccomp, AppArmor or Landlock profile and no no-new-privileges setting was found in this repo; the only trace is the guest kernel argument `lsm=lockdown,capability,landlock,yama,apparmor` (RuntimeService.swift:165-174).

claim_checks.claim: `--publish` forwards traffic from your loopback IP to the container (docs/networking.md:88).
claim_checks.evidence: Without a host-ip the published port binds 0.0.0.0 (Parser.swift:659-672), asserted in Tests/ContainerAPIClientTests/UtilityTests.swift:128 and ParserTest.swift:80,92, and bound at RuntimeService.swift:1028. Loopback binding happens only when `127.0.0.1:` or `[::1]:` is given explicitly. Code wins.

The `container k8s` abstract says '(EXPERIMENTAL)' (Sources/Plugins/K8s/K8sCommand.swift:24); `--masked-path` and `--read-only-path` are also flagged EXPERIMENTAL (Sources/Services/ContainerAPIService/Client/Flags.swift:298-302,347-351).

claim_checks.claim: The `container-apiserver` XPC API keeps forward and backward compatibility within a major version (README.md:106-107).
claim_checks.evidence: No API version field, negotiation or compatibility test was found; the XPC server dispatches on route name and checks only caller EUID (Sources/ContainerXPC/XPCServer.swift:163-205). It is a stated policy only.

claim_checks.claim: Docs state default init/kernel versions (docs/container-system-config.md:44 shows vminit:0.34.0; docs/tutorials/start-here.md:30 shows Kata 3.17.0 .tar.xz).
claim_checks.evidence: Code defaults are Kata 3.32.0 `.tar.zst` with a SHA-256 pin (ContainerSystemConfig.swift:168-171) and a vminit tag derived from scVersion 0.47.0 (ContainerSystemConfig.swift:147-153; Package.swift:26). The kernel entry in container-system-config.md:35 matches the code, but the vminit 0.34.0 example and the tutorial's Kata 3.17.0 are stale. Code wins.

risks: Platform scope: macOS-only. Apple silicon with macOS 26 is the supported target (macOS 15 runs with reduced networking); there is no Linux or WSL2 host path, since the runtime needs Virtualization.framework, vmnet, XPC, launchd and Keychain (README.md:18-20; Package.swift:30; docs/command-reference.md:1327; docs/technical-overview.md:61-75; Sources/Services/NetworkVmnet/Server/ReservedVmnetNetwork.swift:25-26; Sources/ContainerPlugin/ServiceManager.swift:21-45).

No deny-by-default network or egress policy. The built-in `default` network is NAT with outbound access (Sources/APIServer/APIServer+Start.swift:325-331; Sources/ContainerResource/Network/NetworkMode.swift:19-22). `--network none` exists only in code, not in CLI help, docs or tests (Sources/Services/ContainerAPIService/Client/Flags.swift:314; Utility.swift:200-204; NetworkClient.swift:46-47). `network create --internal` relies on vmnet host mode and its only test is flagged intermittent (ReservedVmnetNetwork.swift:114; Tests/IntegrationTests/Network/TestCLINetwork.swift:126-128). No allow-list or firewall code: pf is used only for `--localhost` redirect rules (Sources/Services/ContainerAPIService/Client/PacketFilter.swift:45-73). `-p` without a host IP binds 0.0.0.0 (Parser.swift:659-672).

Filesystem boundary is mount/VM-based, not path-rule-based. The container root is writable unless `--read-only` (docs/resource-usage.md:111-112; Flags.swift:344-345; Sources/ContainerResource/Container/Bundle.swift:143-150). Read-only host binds depend on passing `ro` to the VM mount (Sources/ContainerResource/Container/Filesystem.swift:23-28), and no integration test asserts that a write to a read-only host bind mount fails (Tests/IntegrationTests/Run/TestCLIRunCommand.swift:225-246 only reads; the `:ro` tests in Tests/IntegrationTests/Containers/TestCLIClean.swift:123-167 cover named volumes). `container machine` mounts $HOME read-write by default (docs/command-reference.md:1093); `--ssh` and `--publish-socket` expose host sockets (docs/host-integration.md:8-10; RuntimeService.swift:1170-1193).

Control plane trusts any same-user process. XPC requests are authorized only by matching EUID (Sources/ContainerXPC/XPCServer.swift:175-193) and helpers run in the user's launchd domain (ServiceManager.swift:124-136). No server-side mount or network policy was found (Parser.swift:597-619 validates only existence, client-side), so the apiserver appears to accept whatever mounts a same-user client submits. Some features need sudo and modify host config (/etc/resolver, /etc/pf.conf anchors, mDNSResponder; docs warn the localhost domain disables Private Relay): Sources/ContainerCommands/System/DNS/DNSCreate.swift:56-91; PacketFilter.swift:23-26,112-147; docs/host-integration.md:54-57.

Supply chain and artifact integrity. The in-repo release workflow publishes an unsigned .pkg and a dSYM zip as a draft prerelease; binaries are ad-hoc signed; there are no checksums, notarization, SBOM or attestations; update-container.sh installs a downloaded pkg with sudo and no integrity check beyond HTTPS (.github/workflows/release.yml:44-57; Makefile:34,37,160-173; scripts/update-container.sh:126-160). Runtime artifacts: the vminit and builder images are referenced by mutable tag (ContainerSystemConfig.swift:84-87,147-153), while the Kata kernel is SHA-256 pinned (ContainerSystemConfig.swift:168-171; KernelService.swift:125-131,184-196); the dev-time `make protos` downloads protoc without a checksum (Protobuf.Makefile:28-35).

Resource model and overhead: each container is a VM with defaults of 4 CPUs and 1 GiB (Sources/ContainerPersistence/ContainerSystemConfig.swift:116-117); memory freed in the guest is not returned to macOS (docs/technical-overview.md:55-59); CPU and memory may be overcommitted (docs/resource-usage.md:34-49). No boot-time or overhead measurements are published; the boot-time statement is qualitative only (docs/technical-overview.md:30).

Core isolation behaviour lives in an external, exact-pinned package (apple/containerization 0.47.0): VM boot, vminitd, default masked/read-only paths and capability defaults (Package.swift:26,58; Parser.swift:1093,1099; README.md:10). This dossier did not inspect that package, and masked-path defaults vary with the guest kernel (Tests/IntegrationTests/Run/TestCLIRunSecurityPaths.swift:38-43).

Maintenance, compatibility and scope: versions are 'product versions, not semantic'; app-data compatibility holds only within one major version and experimental features may break (README.md:102-109); docs drift from code (claim check 10); no SECURITY.md or reporting channel (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml:2-5); CI and release run only on Apple's self-hosted macOS runners (.github/workflows/common.yml:25-27); the shallow clone (.git/shallow) prevents assessing commit cadence. It is a general container runtime with no agent-command wrapper, hook or MCP, and Docker features such as compose, restart, commit and attach are absent (skills/container/SKILL.md:38-45).
